ploidyspec report: ddLepDrab1

Summary

Structure in this individual's assembly, read from the sections below; not inheritance and not origin. See docs/guide, Chapter 6.

Ploidy

4 haplotype copies of each of 16 chromosome numbers; the numbers form sets of 2 (8 groups of mostly 2 chromosome numbers), so x ≈ 8 and up to 8x relative to x.

Confidence: high. Evidence: copies from the assembly (4 per number); 8 groups of mostly 2 chromosome numbers (genome partition z = 18.8); homeolog distance 0.069 vs unrelated 0.143

Auto-like or allo-like?

Mixed: tetrasomic-like and split chromosomes in one genome (see rediploidization).

Confidence: medium. Evidence: 16 chromosome numbers assessed: 1 split into lineages, 8 tetrasomic-like, 6 one divergent copy, 1 candidate

TE markers

Repeat history tracks the lineages on 1 chromosome(s) only.

Confidence: low. Evidence: TE split >= 2 on 1/16 chromosomes (median 1.25); absolute te_marker_fraction 0.5465 (reference only)

Rediploidization

Little sign: 1 chromosome(s) partly split among tetrasomic-like ones. Also: homeologous-exchange candidates on 1 chromosome(s), stretches closer to the homeolog than to the own homolog (exchange, or a contig placed on the wrong chromosome).

Confidence: low. Evidence: 1 split / 8 tetrasomic-like chromosomes; 1 regional split(s); residual tetrasomy on 0/16 homeolog-paired chromosome numbers; pair-depth CV 0.06; homeology map: 70% of the genome in 33 homeolog blocks, 8 chromosome pairs, block-divergence CV 0.13; exchange: chr03(chr06:1/4)

Copy number and copy divergence (whole-chromosome matrix)

Hierarchically reordered, chromosome-number resolution

Same distance data as the heatmaps above, but collapsed to one value per chromosome NUMBER (haplotype copies aggregated away) and reordered by average-linkage clustering -- shows cross-chromosome (subgenome/ancestral-pair) structure cleanly, including diffuse structure with no individually FDR-significant pair. Red outlines mark individually FDR-accepted pairs from the homeolog test below. See INTERPRETATION.md's "checkerboard" section.
